textbookText: 5. Intestine: It consists of two partsa. Small Intestine: The small intestine is the long-convoluted tube of 30 cm length in the form of several loops, supported by a fan-like membrane, the mesentery. Small intestine is the main site of digestion and absorption of food. Small intestine consists of duodenum and ileum. i. Duodenum The anterior part of the small intestine which curves upwards to form a U shaped with the stomach is called the duodenum. The internal mucous lining of duodenum is provided with low transverse folds. In the duodenum, opens a common hepato-pancreatic duct from liver and pancreas, draining the bile and pancreatic juice respectively. ii. Ileum The remaining part of small intestine continues as a long, narrow and much twisted tubular part called ileum. The internal mucous layer of

ileum forms a number of longitudinal folds. True villi, glands and crypts are absent. b. Large intestine: The ileum opens into a short and dilated tube of about 4 cm called large intestine or rectum which leads behind into cloacal chamber. Its inner layer is with goblet cells and forms numerous low longitudinal folds. This part absorbs water and stores faeces. 6. Cloacal chamber and cloaca: Rectum is followed by a small terminal sac-like structure, called cloacal chamber. This sac also receives the opening of ureters. Cloacal chamber opens exteriorly through a vent or cloacal opening situated at the posterior most end of the body.

Activity: 8.11 Objective: To identify various parts of buccal cavity in frog Apparatus required: dissecting tray, forceps, needle, chart paper Procedure: i. Take a freshly preserved or chloroformed frog in dissecting tray. ii. Lay down it by facing ventral surface up. iii. Open its mouth and observe. Note down the structures in buccal cavity (take help of teacher if required). iv. Draw well labelled diagram in chart paper and discuss.
In addition to the gastric glands and the intestinal glands, two large digestive glands namely liver and pancreas are also found in frog.

Like other vertebrates, liver in frog, is the largest gland situated in the anterior body cavity close to the heart and lungs. It is reddish brown coloured and lobulated gland consisting of three lobes: - the right, median and the left lobe. The left lobe is again subdivided into two lobes. A spherical, thin-walled, large and greenish sac called gall bladder is present ventrally between the right and left lobe of liver. It serves as a reservoir for the bile juice constantly secreted by the hepatic cells. The bile passes into the gall bladder through hepatic ducts. Cystic duct from gall bladder and some hepatic ducts from liver get united to form a common bile duct which passes through the pancreas and opens into the duodenum. The common bile duct receives the fine ducts from the pancreas while passing on its way to open into duodenum. Bile lacks digestive enzymes.

Histologically, frog’s liver is composed of numerous lobules or hepatic acini and these lobules are separated from each other by the presence of connective tissue containing bile capillaries, hepatic ducts, blood capillaries and sinusoids. Each lobule or hepatic acinus consists of numerous polyhedral, glandular hepatic cells; each containing a nucleus and cytoplasm with protein granules, droplets of fats, glycogen and often black or dark brown pigment granules. Hepatic cells secrete bile juice which is poured into canalicule. These canaliculi unite to form bile ductule which again unite, re-unite and finally form bile or hepatic ducts. The liver receives blood from the hepatic artery and the hepatic portal vein.
